
Two more edge types record identity across a refactor, neither written over `POST /api/v1/rules/{id}/edges`. `wasDerivedFrom` is written by hand with `lode rule link <ref> --derived-from <ref>`; it is an ordinary manual edge with no other writer. `supersedes` runs from the new rule to the old rule it replaces (`dct:replaces`). It has one writer, `lode rule supersede`, and cannot be added or removed any other way. There is no split or merge verb. A split is document-first: editing the document creates the new rule B narrower than A, and an architect records the lineage afterwards with `lode rule link WL-RULE-B --derived-from WL-RULE-A`. A merge is an edit of A that absorbs B's text plus `lode rule supersede` naming `WL-RULE-B -> WL-RULE-A` (a one-line map covers a single pair), which withdraws B and writes `supersedes` from A to B. A keeps its identity and its tasks, and B's tasks resolve to A through the edge (WL-SPEC-77#sec-4bb).
